Corollary
[Embedded Case]

1. ch5:5.30Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and $S\subseteq M$ an embedded submanifold. Every smooth map $F:N\to M$ with $F(N)\subseteq S$ is smooth as an $S$-valued map.

Proof

\sketch Because $S$ has the subspace topology, the subspace universal property (Proposition A.17(a)) first makes $F$ continuous as an $S$-valued map.

□
